sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's technology sector is increasingly driven by domestic digital adoption, with e-commerce and fintech penetration expanding beyond Jakarta into tier-2 cities, creating durable revenue growth
Global AI infrastructure spending continues to lift Indonesian tech hardware and software service providers, as US-listed peers' stability transmits positive sentiment to IDX-listed tech names.
Regulatory clarity on data localization and digital taxation is improving, reducing compliance uncertainty and attracting both foreign portfolio flows and strategic partnerships into the sector.
sectors.ai: Buy selective momentum in ELIT and CENT on strong volume and sector tailwinds, but avoid chasing AREA after its parabolic move. Rotate into JAST and KREN for relative-value upside as US tech stabilizes. Trim NINE and ASGR into strength, as their gains lack fundamental backing. Maintain neutral sector weight, with risk-on bias only for names with clear earnings catalysts.

sectors.name: Financials
themes: US retail trading platforms (HOOD, IBKR) are structurally gaining share via zero-commission and crypto integration, a durable trend that lifts global fintech sentiment and Indonesian digital-brokerage
Indonesia's Sharia-compliant fintech lenders (PADI, AKSI) benefit from rising financial inclusion and Bank Indonesia's digital-payment push, creating sustained loan-growth and fee-income drivers.
Crypto exchange proxies (COIN, BMAS) are leveraged to Bitcoin adoption and US regulatory clarity, but Indonesia's own crypto-tax regime and rupiah volatility cap upside, favoring selective exposure.
sectors.ai: Buy HOOD and COIN on US retail-crypto momentum spillover into Indonesia's digital-asset proxies; PADI and AKSI offer leveraged domestic fintech beta with regulatory tailwinds. Trim BMAS on profit-taking after its run, rotate into IBKR for cross-border volume durability. Watch IDX liquidity—US strength may not translate if rupiah weakens; keep positions under 5% each.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Coal equities are decoupling from thermal price weakness, driven by domestic demand resilience and export logistics advantages, making IDX-listed miners like COAL and DWGL structural outperformers.
Gold and copper miners (EMAS, SMMT, FCX) are benefiting from a persistent US dollar softening and central-bank buying, creating a durable re-rating channel for precious and base metal producers.
The sector's positive signal (WATCH) with US-listed strength (FCX, ALB) indicates global capital is rotating into Indonesian resource names, favoring liquidity and scale over small-cap speculation.
sectors.ai: Buy selective exposure to coal and gold miners on the IDX, led by ALKA and EMAS, as US-listed peers (FCX, ALB) confirm a global commodity bid; rotate from laggards into names with confirmed volume breakouts, targeting a 2-4 week hold as momentum persists, with a stop if the aggregate sector retraces below +0.5%.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's mandatory local-content thresholds for solar and battery components are structurally rerating domestic EPC and cell makers, independent of global clean-tech sentiment.
Falling global polysilicon and module prices are compressing input costs for Indonesian developers, widening margins on fixed-tariff PPAs and accelerating project starts.
US climate-tech names remain hostage to Fed policy and IRA subsidy uncertainty, favoring selective long positions in Indonesian names with domestic revenue visibility over US peers.
sectors.ai: Rotate into Indonesian solar EPC names (POWR, 051910) and domestic battery plays (373220) on tariff-driven local content demand; trim US hydrogen (PLUG) and fuel-cell exposure given rate sensitivity. Watch for Q3 project-award catalysts from RUPTL revisions and IKN green-build tenders, which should sustain momentum into year-end.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rising middle-class disposable income in tier-2/3 cities continues to drive volume growth for affordable packaged foods and beverages, favoring low-priced, high-turnover FMCG names.
Digital distribution and direct-to-consumer channels are structurally lowering go-to-market costs for small-cap consumer brands, enabling faster share gains against incumbents.
Import substitution in packaging and raw materials, supported by government local-content rules, is improving gross margins for domestic producers like YUPI and BTEK.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in small-cap consumer names with confirmed volume (AGAR, YUPI, BTEK) as the sector's relative strength vs. IDX persists; rotate out of laggards into leaders with earnings catalysts. Expect mean-reversion in NAYZ/DAYA after outsized moves—trim into strength. Maintain overweight on staples for defensive positioning ahead of rupiah volatility.

sectors.name: Infrastructure
themes: Indonesia's digital economy expansion drives sustained demand for data-center-linked infrastructure, benefiting tower operators like TOWR and gas suppliers such as RGAS.
Government's push for downstream processing and industrial estates underpins long-term growth for land developers like EKAD and SSIA, supported by FDI inflows.
Packaging and logistics infrastructure names (PACK, PIPA) are riding e-commerce and manufacturing reshoring trends, though valuations require earnings delivery to justify further upside.
sectors.ai: Buy selective infrastructure names with confirmed earnings catalysts: PICO's surge reflects contract wins, while RGAS and TOWR benefit from data-center and tower demand. Favor EKAD and SSIA on industrial-estate and property tailwinds, but avoid chasing PIPA and PACK without volume confirmation. Rotate into laggards with strong cash flows, as sector breadth remains healthy and foreign flows supportive.

sectors.name: Healthcare
themes: US hospital operators benefit from resilient elective-demand volumes and pricing power, sustaining margin expansion into 2025.
Biotech volatility rewards catalyst-driven longs (MRNA, ALNY) as obesity and RNA platforms re-rate on trial readouts.
Indonesia healthcare underperforms due to weak consumer spending and regulatory overhang, favoring selective exposure to private hospitals with high-end demand.
sectors.ai: Buy healthcare selectively: US large-cap operators (HCA, UHS) and biotech catalysts (MRNA, ALNY) are driving outperformance, while Indonesia lags on domestic rotation. Favor US-listed names with earnings momentum and pipeline news; add ZTS for defensive animal-health exposure. Trim Indonesia healthcare until rupiah stabilizes and policy clarity improves.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: Indonesia's port throughput is structurally rising on coal and nickel export quotas, directly lifting PJHB and PORT's terminal-handling fees and utilization rates.
Cold-chain logistics demand is compounding at double digits due to halal food certification and pharmaceutical distribution mandates, underpinning TAMU's recurring contract growth.
US e-commerce parcel density keeps AMKBY's cross-border airfreight and last-mile margins sticky, decoupling it from domestic Indonesia volume cycles.
sectors.ai: Buy PJHB and TAMU on strength from port and cold-chain volume re-rating; trim LOPI into any bounce as its lagging yield signals fading pricing power. Rotate into PORT for toll-road-linked distribution exposure, and hold AMKBY for US e-commerce spillover. Avoid chasing HATM's single-day spike without volume confirmation; keep logistics beta at neutral with selective names only.
